title: Predictive memory pacer and KV guardrails for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem statement: Long-context variants of Llama, Mistral, and Qwen show sporadic GPU memory spikes during continuous batching which lead to OOMs, degraded p99 latency, and excessive CUDA memory fragmentation. Existing per-variant footprint heuristics reduce average memory but do not prevent transient oversubscription when many long-prefixed requests align in the batch. This ticket implements a predictive 'memory pacer' layer and lightweight KV guardrails that coordinate with the continuous batching scheduler and the allocator to smooth memory pressure and avoid spills to host memory.

Goals: implement per-model pacing heuristics that predict near-term KV growth, clamp prefetch and kv-residency allocations dynamically, and add soft-eviction guardrails that free non-critical KV slices when headroom falls below thresholds. The solution should be transparent to the API (no prompt changes), integrate with runtime metrics, and be rollout-safe (canary by model and region).
acceptance_criteria: p99 generation latency does not regress by more than 3% for steady-state throughput
OOM rate for long-context workloads reduced by >95% in staging benchmarks
GPU memory headroom variance reduced (stddev) by >= 40% across 1-minute windows
Canary rollout is implemented and includes automatic fallback to previous allocator behavior
Comprehensive perf dashboards and alerts added for pacer decisions and guardrail triggers
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation — collect per-variant sequence-length histograms, real-time KV growth curves, and batch composition traces (3 days)
Phase 2: Predictor prototype — lightweight linear-predictor using recent token growth + batch size to estimate 1s lookahead memory (4 days)
Phase 3: Pacer integration — wire predictor into batching scheduler to limit batch admission and to control prefetch/kv-residency reservations (5 days)
Phase 4: Guardrails — implement soft-eviction policy for low-importance KV slices and preemptive spill avoidance (4 days)
Phase 5: Benchmarks & canary — run long-dialogue stress tests across Llama-2-7B-chat, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B variants and push canary with runtime-1.20 (3 days)
Phase 6: Rollout — staged rollout with telemetry verification and automatic rollback conditions (2 days)
experiments: Experiment A: No pacer baseline vs pacer-enabled on uniform long-prefix workload (seq=8192) — measure OOMs and p99
Experiment B: Mixed sequence distribution (50% short, 50% long) to validate batch admission thresholds
Experiment C: Aggressive prefetch clamp to validate model-quality impact (sampling with eval promptset)
Experiment D: Interaction with quantized kernels — ensure no perf cliffs when guardrails evict KV pages
comments: 2025-02-15 Marcus Lee: Kickoff — ran initial profiling on a 4-GPU dedicated pool. Observed sustained KV growth when multiple clients sent long-prefixed streaming requests; fragmentation spikes correlated with batch boundary alignment.
2025-02-20 Elena Ortiz: Prototype predictor implemented as exponential-weighted moving average over per-request KV delta. Initial results reduce peak demand by ~30% on Mistral-7B in local sim.
2025-02-24 QA: Found a regression where pacer slightly increases mean latency at very low throughput. We plan to add a grace path that disables pacing when throughput < 5 rps per GPU.
2025-02-28 Performance: Qwen variants show higher sensitivity to prefetch clamps — added an adaptive alpha parameter per-variant (configurable via model profile).
2025-03-03 Devops: Canary config files and rollout script added: canary by model + region with health checks for OOM, p99, and GPU-utilization. PR links below.
